mathleague-2018-19-g5-02.title: Groups of 6
mathleague-2018-19-g5-02.body:
Every group of 6 animals has 5 sheep and 1 cow. $1800 \div 6 = 300$ groups, so there are 1500 sheep and 300 cows. $1500 - 300 = 1200$.

**Answer: (C) 1200**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-02.title: Difference per group
mathleague-2018-19-g5-02.body:
In each group of 6 animals there are $5 - 1 = 4$ more sheep than cows. There are 300 groups, so $300 \times 4 = 1200$ more sheep.

**Answer: (C) 1200**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-03.title: Estimate
mathleague-2018-19-g5-03.body:
The product is about $2000 \times 2000 = 4\,000\,000$, a 7-digit number; the sum is about 4000, a 4-digit number. The difference is 3 digits.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-04.title: Solve for the blank
mathleague-2018-19-g5-04.body:
The left side is 25 000. $(2 \times 50) = 100$, so the second factor must be $25\,000 \div 100 = 250 = 25 \times 10$.

**Answer: (C) 25**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-05.title: Doubling
mathleague-2018-19-g5-05.body:
Doubling a number adds the number itself. Since adding 20 doubles my age, I am 20 now. Two years ago I was 18.

**Answer: (B) 18**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-05.title: Equation
mathleague-2018-19-g5-05.body:
If my age is $a$, then $a + 20 = 2a$, so $a = 20$. Two years ago: $20 - 2 = 18$.

**Answer: (B) 18**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-06.title: Compute
mathleague-2018-19-g5-06.body:
Left side: $2019 - 114 = 1905$. Right side: $2000 - 19 \times ? = 1905$, so $19 \times ? = 95$ and $? = 5$.

**Answer: (B) 5**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-07.title: Spot the 6
mathleague-2018-19-g5-07.body:
$1 \times 2 \times 3 \times 4 \times 5 = 6 \times 20$ (since $2 \times 3 = 6$ and $1 \times 4 \times 5 = 20$). That is 20 periods of 6 days, so 20 cm.

**Answer: (A) 20**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-09.title: Parity
mathleague-2018-19-g5-09.body:
The sum of three even numbers is even, so the perimeter can't be the odd number 9. (The others are possible, e.g. 4+6+6=16, 12+12+12=36, 20+22+22=64.)

**Answer: (A) 9**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-10.title: List them
mathleague-2018-19-g5-10.body:
Primes up to 25: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23. One less: 1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 12, 16, 18, 22. The multiples of 4 are 4, 12 and 16: three numbers.

**Answer: (D) 3**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-10.title: Check multiples of 4
mathleague-2018-19-g5-10.body:
The multiples of 4 below 25 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 (and 0, but 1 is not prime). Add 1: 5 ✓, 9 ✗, 13 ✓, 17 ✓, 21 ✗, 25 ✗. Three work.

**Answer: (D) 3**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-11.title: Per-second rate
mathleague-2018-19-g5-11.body:
10 m per 60 s is $\frac16$ m per second. $8760 \div 6 = 1460$ m.

**Answer: (D) 1460 m**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-12.title: Try Tuesday
mathleague-2018-19-g5-12.body:
If May 1 is a Tuesday, the Mondays are May 7, 14, 21 and 28; the next would be June 4. That is only 4 Mondays, so May 1 can't be a Tuesday.

**Answer: (C) Tuesday**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-12.title: Which days repeat 5 times
mathleague-2018-19-g5-12.body:
May has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days, so the first 3 days of the month are the weekdays that occur 5 times. For Monday to be one of May 1, 2, 3, May 1 must be a Saturday, Sunday or Monday — not a Tuesday.

**Answer: (C) Tuesday**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-13.title: Half the shoe size
mathleague-2018-19-g5-13.body:
Twice the hat size equals 3 times the shoe size, so the hat size is $1\frac12$ times the shoe size. The extra half of the shoe size is 18, so the shoe size is 36 and the hat size is 54. $36 + 54 = 90$.

**Answer: (C) 90**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-13.title: Units
mathleague-2018-19-g5-13.body:
Let the shoe size be 2 units; then 3 times it is 6 units, so the hat size is 3 units. The hat is 1 unit bigger, so 1 unit = 18. Sum $= 5$ units $= 90$.

**Answer: (C) 90**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-14.title: One prime is 2
mathleague-2018-19-g5-14.body:
An odd sum needs one even and one odd number, and the only even prime is 2. So the sum is $2 + p$. $101 = 2 + 99$ but 99 is not prime; $103 = 2 + 101$ and 101 is prime.

**Answer: (B) 103**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-15.title: Compare the parts
mathleague-2018-19-g5-15.body:
Each of the first two km took half as long as the third km, so the first two km together took as long as the third km. The third km is half of the 36 minutes: 18 minutes.

**Answer: (B) 18 minutes**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-15.title: Equation
mathleague-2018-19-g5-15.body:
If the third km took $t$ minutes, each of the first two took $\frac t2$. $\frac t2 + \frac t2 + t = 2t = 36$, so $t = 18$.

**Answer: (B) 18 minutes**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-16.title: Smallest and largest factor
mathleague-2018-19-g5-16.body:
The smallest factor of any whole number is 1 and the greatest is the number itself. $1 + 2019 = 2020$.

**Answer: (C) 2020**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-17.title: Per day
mathleague-2018-19-g5-17.body:
3 hours 2 minutes = 182 minutes of games in 7 days, so $182 \div 7 = 26$ minutes per day on average. Homework is twice that: 52 minutes.

**Answer: (D) 52 minutes**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-17.title: Week first
mathleague-2018-19-g5-17.body:
Weekly homework is twice the gaming: $2 \times 182 = 364$ minutes. $364 \div 7 = 52$ minutes per day.

**Answer: (D) 52 minutes**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-18.title: Use 9s
mathleague-2018-19-g5-18.body:
The largest a ones digit can be is 9, so the largest product is $9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 9 = 6561$ (for example, with 9, 19, 29, 39).

**Answer: (D) 6561**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-19.title: Spread the loss
mathleague-2018-19-g5-19.body:
Pulling the average of 3 games down by 5 points takes $3 \times 5 = 15$ points in total. The first two games were at the old average, so the third game must have been 15 points below that average.

**Answer: (C) 15**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-19.title: Try numbers
mathleague-2018-19-g5-19.body:
Say the first two games were 50 and 50 (average 50). The new average is 45, so the total of 3 games is 135 and the third game is $135 - 100 = 35$, which is 15 below 50.

**Answer: (C) 15**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-20.title: Scale up
mathleague-2018-19-g5-20.body:
If she shelled 1 nut on day 1, she would shell $1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15$ nuts in 4 days. She actually shelled $360 \div 15 = 24$ times as many: 24 on day 1 and $8 \times 24 = 192$ on day 4. $192 - 24 = 168$.

**Answer: (B) 168**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-20.title: Units
mathleague-2018-19-g5-20.body:
Day 1 = 1 unit, then 2, 4, 8 units: 15 units = 360, so 1 unit = 24. Day 4 minus day 1 = $8 - 1 = 7$ units $= 168$.

**Answer: (B) 168**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-22.title: Square of a prime
mathleague-2018-19-g5-22.body:
A number with exactly 3 factors is the square of a prime: its factors are 1, $p$, $p^2$. The middle factor is 7, so the number is $49$. Digit sum $4 + 9 = 13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-22.title: Pair the factors
mathleague-2018-19-g5-22.body:
Factors pair up as (factor, number ÷ factor). With 3 factors, one must pair with itself, so the number is a square. The factors are 1, 7, and the number, so the number is $7 \times 7 = 49$; $4 + 9 = 13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-23.title: Complement
mathleague-2018-19-g5-23.body:
There are $6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$ possible numbers. Those with three *different* digits: $6 \times 5 \times 4 = 120$. So $216 - 120 = 96$ have at least two identical digits.

**Answer: (A) 96**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-23.title: Count directly
mathleague-2018-19-g5-23.body:
All three digits equal: 6 numbers. Exactly two equal: choose the repeated digit (6), the other digit (5), and the position of the odd one out (3): $6 \times 5 \times 3 = 90$. Total $6 + 90 = 96$.

**Answer: (A) 96**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-24.title: Use the largest 2-digit number
mathleague-2018-19-g5-24.body:
Each 2-digit number is at most 99. Twenty of them add to at most $20 \times 99 = 1980 < 2019$, so at least 21 are needed. Since $21 \times 99 = 2079 > 2019$, 21 is enough.

**Answer: (B) 21**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-25.title: Share the extra boys
mathleague-2018-19-g5-25.body:
Each group can hold at most 2 of the 7 extra boys. Three groups hold at most 6 extra boys, so at least 4 groups are needed, and 4 works: split the extra boys 2, 2, 2, 1.

**Answer: (B) 4**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-26.title: Count with powers of 2
mathleague-2018-19-g5-26.body:
An even factor uses at least one 2. $4 = 2^2$: choices $2^1, 2^2$ → 2. $80 = 2^4 \times 5$: $4 \times 2 = 8$. $100 = 2^2 \times 5^2$: $2 \times 3 = 6$. $128 = 2^7$: 7 (odd).

**Answer: (D) 128**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-27.title: Bottom half
mathleague-2018-19-g5-27.body:
There are 12 competitors behind Kaz. Counting Kaz and the 3 competitors between him and the top half, the bottom half has $3 + 1 + 12 = 16$ places. So the top half is also 16, Kaz is in place $16 + 4 = 20$, and 19 placed ahead of him.

**Answer: (B) 19**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-27.title: Equation
mathleague-2018-19-g5-27.body:
With $N$ competitors, Kaz is in place $N - 12$ and also in place $\frac N2 + 4$. So $N - 12 = \frac N2 + 4$, giving $N = 32$ and Kaz's place $= 20$. 19 people were ahead.

**Answer: (B) 19**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-28.title: List factors
mathleague-2018-19-g5-28.body:
$2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30$, whose factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Their sum is 72 and there are 8 of them, so the average is $72 \div 8 = 9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-28.title: Factor sum shortcut
mathleague-2018-19-g5-28.body:
The sum of factors of $2 \times 3 \times 5$ is $(1+2)(1+3)(1+5) = 3 \times 4 \times 6 = 72$, and the number of factors is $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$. $72 \div 8 = 9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-29.title: Middle number
mathleague-2018-19-g5-29.body:
For consecutive numbers, the average is the middle number. The middle of 99 numbers is the 50th, so the 50th number is 100, with 49 numbers before it. The first number is $100 - 49 = 51$, and $5 + 1 = 6$.

**Answer: (B) 6**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-29.title: Pair up
mathleague-2018-19-g5-29.body:
If the first number is $f$, the numbers run from $f$ to $f + 98$, and the average is $f + 49 = 100$. So $f = 51$; digit sum 6.

**Answer: (B) 6**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-30.title: Find the number
mathleague-2018-19-g5-30.body:
$n \times n = 24 \times n$, so $n = 24$. The sum is $24 \times 24 = 576$ and half of it is 288.

**Answer: (D) 288**

mathleague-2018-19-g5-30.title: Work from the choices
mathleague-2018-19-g5-30.body:
The sum is a perfect square, so double each choice and look for a square: 96, 288, 480, 576. Only $576 = 24 \times 24$ is a square (and it equals $24 \times 24$ written as 24 copies of 24). Half is 288.

**Answer: (D) 288**
